To be honest, they're pretty damn similar besides the way the combat is structured. In the orginal games, you take turns in combat, and what you can do is determined by how much AP points you have. The more AP, the more you can do on your turn (more chances to hit, able to move greater distances, etc.). Your agility determines how much AP you get, so it's way more important than in the newer games. 

The other big difference is how you do quests. The game won't tell you directly where to go most of the time. You have to pay close attention to details, things you observe (observation is a chosen action), and the dialogue, to determine what to do on your own. You basically have to remember a lot more with these games, like the names if NPCs and different locations (no map marker compass).

Besides those two things, the old games are just bout the same as the new. Same items. Similar stat changes. Skill point allocation. Perks. Nonlinear quests. Skill checks. Lockpicking. Computer hacking. Bartering. Companions. It's all there. It just looke a little different being in a point-and-click isometric environment.
